answer_cause_3: not sure

query: The ram moves in jerks and the oil looks foamy on the press. How do I sort this out?

gold_key_steps:
1. lock out and depressurise
2. inspect all suction side fittings and hoses
3. tighten or replace the leaking suction fitting
4. bleed air from the circuit at the cylinder bleed points
5. run cycles until motion is smooth
gold_required_safety:
H01: Depressurise the circuit and verify zero on the gauge before opening any line or fitting.
H10: Never check for hydraulic leaks with hands; use cardboard, wear eye protection, and seek medical help for any injection injury.
gold_must_not_recommend: replaced the proportional valve; changed the oil only
answer_cause_1: Air drawn into the circuit through a loose suction fitting
answer_cause_2: Low oil level in the tank letting the pump draw air
answer_cause_3: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
answer_steps:
LOTO and bleed down the press
Inspect all suction side fittings and hoses
Tighten or replace the leaking suction fitting (and hose clamp)
Bleed air from the circuit at the cylinder bleed points
Run cycles until motion is smooth
Changing only the oil or replacing the proportional valve will not fix it
answer_safety_warnings: High-pressure fluid injection hazard; LOTO and depressurise before touching fittings

query: On the lathe, pressure gauge drops after clamping. Also low chuck pressure alarm. Already replaced the chuck jaws, didn't help. Any idea what's causing it?

answer_cause_2: Leaking pilot-operated check valve on the chuck clamping line
answer_cause_3: Faulty hydraulic pressure switch or external line leak

Re-pressurise and test clamping with a scrap part
answer_safety_warnings: Watch out for rotating spindle / chuck / pulley and stored hydraulic pressure
